leftEvidence.title: Israel’s affliction leads to Moses’ commission

points.label: Israel setting and claim
points.left: The LORD says Israel’s affliction is seen and its cry heard, promises descent and deliverance, and sends Moses to Pharaoh.
points.right: The LORD tells Moses what to say to Pharaoh and names Israel as son and firstborn.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Moses asks who he is and what divine name he should give the people.
points.right: refusal to release that son is answered with a threat against Pharaoh’s firstborn.

payload.posture: Moses’ commission and the firstborn declaration interpret the confrontation with Pharaoh through relationship as well as liberation.

rightEvidence.title: Israel is called God’s son and firstborn

payload.tension: One passage stresses seen suffering and a sent messenger; the other compresses sonship, demand, refusal, and threatened death.
payload.title: A suffering people named as a son
